conventions.convention: Time starts at zero. A test supermartingale is real-valued, adapted, integrable and nonnegative almost surely at each time under every null law, satisfies the supermartingale condition under each such law, and has initial expectation at most one; its initial value need not be pointwise bounded by one.
Discrete stopping times take values in N₀ ∪ {∞}; their event tests are literal, without assuming a completed filtration. The infimum of an empty set of hitting times is ∞.
AC is assumed explicitly through the conditional-expectation, test-supermartingale and optional-sampling suppliers.
The supremum event uses ≥ 1/α and is distinct from finite-time threshold attainment. The event involving Mσ is restricted to σ < ∞.
Repeated peeking uses K ≥ 2 mutually independent uniform p-values, α ∈ (0,1), and a filtration that is trivial at zero and constant after look K.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. Let P₀ be a family of probability laws and M = (M_t) indexed by N₀ be a nonnegative test supermartingale for P₀. For every P ∈ P₀, every a > 0, and every N ∈ N₀, P(max_{0≤t≤N} M_t ≥ a) ≤ E_P M₀/a ≤ 1/a.

Assume AC. For a nonnegative test supermartingale M for a family P₀, every P ∈ P₀ and α ∈ (0,1), define τα = inf{t ≥ 0 : M_t ≥ 1/α}, with inf ∅ = ∞. Then P(sup_{t≥0} M_t ≥ 1/α) ≤ α and P(τα < ∞) ≤ α. Moreover, for every discrete stopping time σ, P(σ < ∞, Mσ ≥ 1/α) ≤ α, where the event involving Mσ is restricted to {σ < ∞}.

published_dependencies.used_for: Identifies the explicit choice assumption inherited through conditional expectation and optional sampling.
Zero-based discrete filtrations without completeness or initial triviality requirements; verifies the counterexample's refining partitions.
Checks the counterexample's conditional means by event integrals on the finite partition atoms.
Interprets the counterexample's conditional-expectation identities as almost-sure identities and records inherited AC.
Checks the adjacent-time martingale condition in the counterexample and the supermartingale convention.
Supplies the common-process, per-null-law conditions and initial expectation normalization.
Checks first rejection times, bounded truncation, and measurability at finite stopping times.
Makes the first hit of the Borel set [a,∞) a stopping time in the finite-horizon lemma.
Gives E_P M_{τa∧N} ≤ E_P M₀ for the supermartingale, including N = 0.
Interprets expectations and verifies integrability of the bounded counterexample process.
Applies almost-sure expectation monotonicity and scalar linearity to the stopped process lower bound.
Converts the expected crossing-event indicator into its probability.
Passes from increasing finite-horizon crossing events to the all-time crossing event.
Fixes mutual independence of the repeated-look p-values.
Computes the probability of no rejection as (1−α)^K.
Checks the explicitly weighted countable probability space of the counterexample.
Bounds the counterexample process expectations using nonnegative integral monotonicity and positive homogeneity.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier's full finite-horizon and Ville arguments against thm-subgaussian-mixture-confidence-sequence F4 and Proof 3.1. The consumer explicitly assumes AC, fixes each parameter law separately, and uses a nonnegative test supermartingale with M₀ = 1 supplied by thm-gaussian-mixture-test-supermartingale. Exclusion from its closed interval implies a threshold crossing and hence membership in the supremum event bounded by Ville. The α domain, discrete-time scope, singleton-null application and nonattained-supremum distinction are preserved.
